lessons: CRITICAL FIX: the Shaagat HaAri emergency chal"t window CLOSED. BTL states verbatim 'על פי החוק, המתווה בתוקף (בתקופת החירום) - עד 14.4.2026' with a possible one-month extension to 14.5.2026. The skill still presented the 6-of-18 qualifying route as available. A July-2026 claimant with 7-11 salaried months could have been told they qualify when they do not.

CRITICAL FIX: the 90-day resignation clock was documented backwards. BTL states 'אם הפסקת לעבוד מרצונך תוכל להתחיל לקבל דמי אבטלה רק לאחר שחלפו 90 יום מיום הפסקת העבודה' - counted from the day work ceased. The skill said it runs from the registration date in five places, and Gotcha #10 explicitly labelled the CORRECT rule a mistake. Fixed in SKILL.md, SKILL_HE.md and references/eligibility-rules.md.

ADDED: the 3-of-18 qualifying tier for special populations inside the same window (operation evacuees; people on a BL or MoD disability allowance; spouses of reservists with 90+ days in the preceding year; MoD-recognised hostile-action casualties and disabled IDF veterans since 7 Oct and their spouses; soldiers discharged within the last year), each with its required attachment, paid in full with no 5-day deduction. It was absent from every file, so an eligible claimant in one of those groups would have been told they failed the qualifying period.

THE REPEATED PROCESS FAILURE: the first pass of this cycle put the closure statement in ONE paragraph of Special Cases and nowhere else. The frontmatter, metadata description, Problem statement, Step 1 intake, the Step 2 eligibility gate, Step 7, Troubleshooting, both reference files and the calculator all still offered the dead track. This is the same old-value-propagation failure that hit israeli-miluim-manager in the immediately preceding update. The rule to apply BEFORE running the review panel: after changing any rule or figure, grep the old value across the entire folder, including metadata.json, evidence.json, every reference and every script, and require zero unqualified hits.

CODE MUST ENFORCE TEMPORAL RULES, NOT COMMENTS: scripts/avtala_calculator.py accepted --emergency-chalat with no date input at all and would print [ELIGIBLE] for a 7-month claimant today. Added EMERGENCY_WINDOW_START/END constants and a --chalat-start flag; the emergency track is now a hard error when the date is missing or outside the window. A closed track documented only in prose is not closed.

Evidence hygiene: 41 of ~63 entries failed --check-sources because their snippets were paraphrases or carried 'URL: ...' prefixes rather than quotations. 24 were auto-repaired by locating the longest genuine substring actually present on the cited page; 6 that were the skill's own worked-example arithmetic were removed as evidence and replaced by a single entry explicitly marked claim_type 'derived'; the rest were re-anchored to page titles or real quotes.

PERCENT-ENCODED URL TRAP, hit again: fully percent-encoding a Hebrew kolzchut URL produced phantom percentage claims (28%, 22%, 92%, 97%) because adjacent %XX%XX sequences read as 'NN%'. The fix is to keep the Hebrew literal and encode ONLY the delimiters that truncate URL extraction (parentheses and the gershayim), as in .../he/דמי_אבטלה_..._%28חל%22ת%29_....

CARRY (verify, do not guess): the expert review flagged that Form 126 may be the wrong claimant-side document (it is the employer's annual consolidated report; the employee's annual summary is 106, and BL's own set is likely אישור מעסיק 1514 plus payslips). The skill asserts Form 126 as mandatory in four places and builds Gotcha #11 around it. Not changed this cycle because it was not verified against BTL's document list.

CARRY (verify, do not guess): the skill states in five places that an in-person Sherut HaTaasuka visit within 14 days is constitutive and that missing it voids the registration. The expert believes this is obsolete post-COVID. Note the skill itself records that branches were closed for six weeks in 2026 with rights preserved, which sits awkwardly with the rule being constitutive. Verify on taasuka.gov.il.

CARRY: the 5-day deduction appears only as a contrast column in the emergency-track comparison table. It is never defined or quantified on the standard track, and the calculator does not subtract it, so projected totals overstate the first payment. Add it as its own subsection in the amount step and deduct it in the script.

CARRY: payment in lieu of prior notice (דמי הודעה מוקדמת) is absent from every file. For the skill's single most common fact pattern, a worker fired after two years, it moves the benefit start date by roughly a month.

CARRY: הבטחת/השלמת הכנסה is presented as simply 'stackable' with a typical ₪1,500-2,000/month. It is a separate means-tested benefit where avtala counts as income and household income, assets and vehicle tests all gate it. Reframe as conditional and source or drop the shekel range.

CARRY: the appeal route (informal ועדת תביעות within 6 months, then labour court within 12 months, plus a 60-day ועדת עררים window) is unsourced and may conflate the disability-track institution with the avtala route. Verify each row; lead with the labour-court deadline.

CARRY: age bands in the max-days prose overlap at the boundaries (20-25 / 25-28 / 28-35 ...), so someone exactly 28 matches two rows. The calculator resolves this correctly with half-open intervals; only the prose is ambiguous.

Confirmed correct and not to be re-litigated: the 2026 brackets (80/50/45/30 for 28+, reduced set under 28), the 550.76 and 367.17 daily ceilings with the step-down at day 126, the wage divisor of 150, and the women 57-67 300-day track including the 201.03 day-176 cap that applies to ages 57-60 but not 60-67. Both worked examples recompute exactly.

This cycle's defects were all COVERAGE, not wrong values: every figure the skill stated was correct, and what was missing were rows. Enumerating each BTL table in full is what found them; spot-checking the stated values would have passed cleanly.

references/application-forms.md is the file this skill's corrections keep missing. In 1.6.2 the '75% of the part-time gross' factor and the '25% of prior wage / 60-minute commute' suitability test were retracted in the CHANGELOG and fixed in two files but left live in that one for a full version. Both reviewers found it again this cycle. Read that file FIRST next time, before touching SKILL.md.

Two prior cycles' retractions were also still live elsewhere: the Sefer HaChukim 3525 citation in benefit-calculation-tables.md and the s.174 postponement rule inside the same file that elsewhere said s.174 is NOT that rule. Grep the CHANGELOG's own retraction list against the tree at the START of a cycle.

The calculator carried a note stating the 90-day resignation clock runs from the REGISTRATION date, the exact opposite of the skill body, the reference file and BTL's wording. Prose-vs-code drift in an 'evergreen' deterministic script.

Expert MAJOR resolved this cycle, not deferred: hefreshim (retroactive differentials) was absent from all six files despite sitting at the bottom of hisuv.aspx, the page the skill cites for its own formula. Read the WHOLE cited page, not the section you came for.

The unemployment-branch treaty is only Austria, the Netherlands and Sweden. The skill (and the research subagent's first draft) carried the 15-country GENERAL social-security treaty list. A returning Israeli from the US would have been routed to a guaranteed refusal. Branch scope is not treaty scope.

Deferred, MINOR: estimate_net() applies an invented 0/5/10% income-tax step function by daily-gross thresholds of 400 and 500, disclosed only by the generic 'estimates' footer while the health component gets an explicit NET CAVEAT. Either caveat the tax ladder the same way or flatten it to 0 with a 'consult your marginal rate' note.

Deferred, MINOR: 'refused-offer' is modelled as a termination reason, so a claimant who was laid off AND later refused an offer cannot express both. It is a mid-claim event and wants its own repeatable flag.
Deferred, MINOR: evidence.json has no per-claim verified flag; unverifiable items are segregated into a separate array, so a claim dropping out of both arrays would be invisible.
